newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bond countertrend rally prompts caution.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bond countertrend rally prompts caution.

text.p: A fairly strong rally in U.S. Treasury bond futures early on Tuesday has improved the market's near-term technical picture, although it would likely be a short-lived, countertrend spike, analysts said.

"What you have to realize is that this is largely a situation augmented by short-covering," said Eric Marshall Wall, a technical analyst at MMS International. "Nonetheless, from a technical standpoint, the market is long overdue for some meaningful correction."
June futures hit a high of 107-23/32, up 1-1/32 point, after a softer than expected March consumer price index.

The overall CPI for March rose 0.1 percent against economists' average forecast of a 0.2 percent gain, and the core CPI excluding food and energy climbed 0.2 percent versus an estimated rise of 0.3 percent.
"We wouldn't have normally gotten a move this strong had the market not been so short," Wall said.

But given the market's heavily oversold condition, corrective upward pressure should gather steam if the June contract rises above various minor resistance between 107-22/32 and 107-28/32 and punches through the March 20 low of 107-31/32, he said.
Then, he said, the move could become a tradable rally for people outside the day-trading circle, with a target of 109-7/32, the 38-percent retracement of the decline from the mid-February highs.

But Wall stressed that the trend had not been dramatically changed, adding that a failure to take out the resistance zone just below 108 could quickly lead to a retest of mid-1996 lows in the 105-28/32 to 106-00 area on a continuous chart basis.
Stewart Taylor of Taylor Consulting said he preferred playing a rally here by reducing short exposures to keep the powder dry for an eventual resumption of the downtrend.
"It will leave us short, but we'll be able to replace some shorts at higher levels," he said.
"One day does not a bull market make," he said, adding that the Commodity Research Bureau index rose on Monday.
"I have a hard time viewing that as a positive," he said.

He said there could be some lateral, grinding move around current levels for a while, given the conflict between the prevailing downtrend and strong support in the 106-area, which coincides with cash bond yield levels of 7-1/4 percent.
"Even if the trend is in the process of changing, odds are pretty good that we'll get some sort of a move lower to retest the areas of the lows before we go higher again," he said.
In Eurodollar futures, Wall said a rise in the September contract above April highs in the 93.75 area could open the way for further gains of about 10 basis points.
But he warned that the contract would be targetting Fibonacci extensions at 93.58 and 93.50 once it started closing below April lows in the 93.63 area.
September Euros stood at 93.705, up 0.060 in late morning trade.
